voice: An oily, wheedling stool pigeon and huckster: boastful, self-serving, and quick to flirt with 'toots,' but cowardly and evasive when cornered. Heavy contractions, 1920s slang, and malapropisms; a light touch of accent ('ain't,' 'ya,' 'gonna,' 'dunno,' dropped g's) but no phonetic respellings such as 'dat' or 'hoid.' Flirting sits between vanilla and the P2-08 rewrite. Maintainer direction, 2026-10-14; supersedes the earlier P2-08 Ziggy voice.

entries.text: Who sent ya?
Never heard of 'em, toots. Amscray.
Crodfoller? He's an old pal of mine. Whatcha wanna know?
Ya mean The Sun Also Rises, his novel of postwar disillusion? Sure! Ernest and me go way back! He ran that book by me before it ever got published, and I told him it's a real corker!
I don't talk to strangers, toots.
I ain't got all day to shoot the breeze, toots. You got some specific questions to ask me?
Don't touch me, toots. Not till we're better acquainted, anyway.
That's me. Ya wanna make somethin' of it?
Crodfoller? He's an old pal of mine. Whatcha wanna know?
That's today's password. And it's a swell dance.
Uhh, I think he's a cop.
That name rings a bell. I think he works on the docks.
That's the guy who does my laundry.
That's the guy who found that fancy pigsticker in Egypt.
That's the new president of the Leyendecker Museum.
Never heard that name before, toots.
I heard somebody heisted that Egyptian pigsticker from the museum. Word on the street is it was an inside job.
The pigsticker? Somebody heisted it.
Do I look like an encyclopedia? I don't know nothin' about that.
What makes ya think I know anything about police stations? Ya think I'm a hood or somethin'? I got friends in high places, toots, so don't mess with me!
That's where my pal Crodfoller works.
That's the docks, down at the end of Twelfth Street.
Why ya showin' me that?
That's the accountant from the museum. Spooky, high-hat kinda guy.
I think it was a great year! I made a sawbuck on the Tunney-Dempsey fight in Philly!
It's the place to be. All kinds come here, like one big smeltin' pot. There's even a high-class international con man in town, but I can't tell ya who, 'cause he'd kill me if he found out.
All I know is that Egyptian pigsticker got heisted from the museum.
The only Egyptian I know is an accountant named Rameses Najeer. He bugs me sometimes, askin' me riddles. I can never figure 'em out.

Well, today Rameses came in and asked me a two-part riddle: "What is the room you leave without entering?" and "What is the room you enter without leaving?" As usual, I told him I didn't give a hoot about his silly questions, so he left.
Ya mean this speakeasy? It's the best in town, and I oughta know. I been to all of 'em.
Yvette? Swell girl. We knew each other before she went to work at the museum, if ya catch my drift. She's respectable now, and I'm way too discreet to say more.
The Countess? Real classy dame. Real dangerous, too. If she asks, we never met.
